Hello Everyone, 

In my own voyage into AI coverage and curation of the last three years, I have been reluctant to cover “AI Tools” in spite of its popularity among AI Newsletter Creators. I’m a pragmatist, and frankly a lot of the AI tools in 2023 were simply not that good or refined. Many that I tried didn’t do what they claimed to be able to do and weren’t that useful. 

But slowly as times goes on, in 2024 or looking ahead to 2025, we will begin to see sustainable use cases with improved category leaders for enterprise applications and enhancements in real-world use cases for works settings, task automation, time saving and performance enhancement (even if in limited ways). This means I’ll be starting to cover more AI Tools in this Newsletter.  Before Agentic AI begins to impress, the first wave of Generative AI tools are improving. 

If you’d like to get the best of what I offer in this domain: 

Support and Dive Deeper

Support my work for as little as $2 a week. 🎓📚💡

Subscribe

Full disclosure: I have zero affiliate links in this article. 

While I am skeptical that AI boosts productivity, or will anytime soon in an economically meaningful way for the collective as is claimed in the marketing of several major corporations, that doesn’t mean as workers, leaders and CEOs we cannot adopt some of these AI tools in our own lives, workflows and daily tasks. 

Learning AI Tools with a Health Skepticism 

For the record, I am not a big believer in Copilots, Chatbots or “GPT Stores”, but that doesn’t mean skipping learning, not adapting and not investing some time, effort and curiosity to try the best of them. 

If we are optimists, we might believe that we are about to enter a period where “Agentic AI” might actually make some real headway with AI boosting productivity, time will tell. This might also turn out to be a fad, gimmick and a disappointing marketing narrative. 

In critical areas like in coding and for software engineers, this (productivity improvements) is already the case in mid 2024. In this article I’ll cover some tools and industries and try to help you adapt your way of thinking about this, in case you feel behind the curve.

What can AI Do Again?

Zoom in: (View on Desktop) 

Image: Kelvin Mu, LinkedIn. 

While we should be skeptical of AI boosting us at work, imagining how it might improve our performance, even on an individual basis and in narrow ways is fascinating and worthy of careful consideration and outright speculation, experimentation and for some of us, determined trial and error. Chances are, you’ve already tested this for tasks you do a lot each week. 

How can Generative AI Help Professionals be More Productive?

Some of these will sound broad and generic, but think about how your work-life workflows actually work and how much time can be saved with the right tools. 

◾ More efficient communication and collaboration

◾ Quicker admin and internal comms

◾ Eliminating or helping to speed up/automate repetitive tasks

◾ Code suggestion, translation and improvement (software-editing)

◾ Code testing and bug detection 

◾ Personalized development environments and enhanced documentation

◾ Automated and AI-assisted customer service and customer success 

◾ Time management: smart scheduling and meeting note documentation 

◾ Writing, editing and Email management assistance 

◾ Research, product ideation, and brainstorming 

◾ And so many other interesting uses cases that are starting to become valid for particular industries like software engineers, legal professionals, academics or healthcare clinicians and physicians.
